deep.reconstruction:
This is a scratch slip next to a fundamental-theorem-of-algebra argument. The previous page proves that |Omega(x)| attains a minimum inside a disc. Here a concrete septic family is set up, in which only the constant term varies along a closed curve.

Line 1: x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 + 200 cos(psi) = 0. A word before cos is struck out. The angle psi is evidently meant to be complex.

Marginal note: sqrt(1.4^2 - 1). Here 1.4 = 280/200. Write cosh(alpha) = 1.4 (my notation). Then sinh(alpha) = sqrt(0.96) = 0.9798 and 200 sinh(alpha) = sqrt(38400) = 195.959.

Line 2: x^7 - 28x^4 + 280 - 280 cos(phi) - i sin(phi) sqrt(38400) = 0. A miswritten factor before i is struck out. This is line 1 with psi = pi - phi + i*alpha (the substitution is my reconstruction). Then
 200 cos(psi) = -200(cos(phi) cosh(alpha) + i sin(phi) sinh(alpha)) = -280 cos(phi) - i sqrt(38400) sin(phi).

So the constant term c(phi) = 280 - 280 cos(phi) - i*195.96 sin(phi) traces an ellipse:
- centre 280;
- semi-axes 280 and 195.96;
- since 280^2 - 38400 = 200^2, foci at 80 and 480;
- it passes through c = 0 (phi = 0) and c = 560 (phi = pi).

I note, without certainty, that x^7 - 28x^4 + 480 may be the septic Gauss used as an example in his FTA work. The real critical values of x^7 - 28x^4 + c are c = 0 and c = 12*16^(4/3) ≈ 483.8, the latter close to 480.

Lines 3-5: the ellipse point is evaluated at cos(phi) = ∓1/sqrt(2), sin(phi) = 1/sqrt(2), i.e. phi = 135° or 45°.
- Real part: 280 ± 280/sqrt(2) = 280 ± sqrt(39200), with sqrt(39200) = 197.9898987.
- Imaginary part: -i sqrt(38400)/sqrt(2) = -i sqrt(19200).
- Gauss writes 138.9244399 for sqrt(19200).
- He then writes 2.1416506, which is log10(sqrt(19200)) = (1/2) log10(19200), presumably taken from log tables in preparation for computing the roots.

Purpose: tracing roots of the septic as the constant term runs round this ellipse, presumably to illustrate the root-existence / continuity argument. The roots themselves are not computed on this slip.
errors: 138.9244399 is sqrt(19300), not sqrt(19200) = 138.5640646. However, the logarithm 2.1416506 that follows is correct for sqrt(19200), so the slip affects only the written decimal value (likely a table or copying error).
Struck-out symbols in lines 1 and 2 (before cos and before i sin) are false starts, corrected on the page.
